**1 — Scene:** Rice with two pieces of cooked, bone-in chicken and two corn-on-the-cob rounds.

**2 — Vessel:** A square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Allowing for its rounded square shape, use an equivalent circular diameter of about 27 cm: area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ **572 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Cooked, lightly browned rice; chicken with some skin and cooking juices; corn rounds. No clearly separate oil or sauce portion is visible.

**4 — Area:** Rice covers approximately 20%, chicken 18%, and corn 9%: **47% total coverage**, consistent with the substantial exposed plate.

| Item | Area | Average height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked rice | 114 cm² | 2.0 cm | 228 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 182 g | 145 | 264 kcal |
| Bone-in chicken | 103 cm² | 2.0 cm | 206 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 196 g | 145 | 284 kcal |
| Corn rounds, including cob | 52 cm² | 1.5 cm | 78 ml | 0.7 g/ml | 55 g | 65 | 36 kcal |

Chicken and corn weights include the visible bones and cobs; their energy densities are correspondingly lower than those of edible meat or kernels alone. No additional volume reduction is applied.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **433 g as plated and 584 kcal** is plausible for the visible rice, two chicken pieces, and two small corn rounds. Thickness and bone content are the largest uncertainties.
